title_en: Zhanjiang Xiqiang Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. v. Suixi County Housing, Urban and Rural Planning and Construction Bureau et al. — dispute over the formulation and approval of a general land use plan
ruling_gist_en: Regarding the justiciability of an urban master plan, the implementation of the master plan's content remains uncertain and requires implementation through detailed plans, particularly construction detailed plans, and further materialization through the 'one document and two permits' system. If a party believes that the content of the master plan infringes upon its lawful rights and interests, it should seek relief through the objection procedures for the detailed plans implementing the master plan, especially the construction detailed plans, and through the judicial review procedures for administrative acts granting or denying the 'one document and two permits.' Supervision of the master plan may be carried out through democratic deliberation procedures as provided in Article 16 of the Urban and Rural Planning Law, as well as through professional judgment and public participation, but should not be subject to supervision through judicial review procedures.

full_text_en:
Zhanjiang Xiqiang Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. v. Suixi County Housing and Urban-Rural Planning and Construction Bureau et al. — dispute over formulation and approval of overall land use planning

【Ruling Summary】

With respect to the justiciability of an overall urban planning, the implementation of its content remains uncertain and requires detailed planning, especially constructive detailed planning, to be carried out, and further needs to be concretized through "one document and two permits." A party who believes that the content of an overall planning infringes upon its lawful rights and interests shall seek relief through the objection procedures against the detailed planning that implements the overall planning, especially the constructive detailed planning, and through the judicial review procedure for the administrative act of issuing or not issuing the "one document and two permits." The supervision of overall planning may be conducted both through democratic deliberation procedures as provided in Article 16 of the Urban and Rural Planning Law, and through procedures such as professional judgment and public participation, but it is not appropriate to exercise supervision through judicial review procedures.

Supreme People's Court Administrative Ruling

(2019) Supreme People's Court Administrative Application No. 10407

Re-applicant (plaintiff at first instance, appellant at second instance): Zhanjiang Xiqiang Industrial Gas Co., Ltd., domiciled at: opposite Ganling Sugar Refinery, No. 374 Provincial Road, Lingbei Town, Suixi County, Guangdong Province.

Legal representative: Xu Chengxi, General Manager of the company.

Respondent (defendant at first instance, appellee at second instance): Suixi County Housing and Urban-Rural Planning and Construction Bureau, domiciled at: No. 18 Dongshan Road, Suicheng Town, Suixi County, Guangdong Province.

Legal representative: Wang Yonglong, Director of the bureau.

Respondent (defendant at first instance, appellee at second instance): Suixi County People's Government, domiciled at: No. 133 Zhongshan Road, Suixi County, Guangdong Province.

Legal representative: Yu Qingchuang, County Magistrate.

Third party at first instance: Guangdong Beibu Gulf Agricultural Products Wholesale Center Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Second Floor, Office Building of Jinling Sugar Refinery, Lingbei Town, Suixi County, Guangdong Province.

Legal representative: Lin Decai, Chairman of the company.

The re-applicant, Zhanjiang Xiqiang Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company), appealed against the administrative ruling of the Guangdong High People's Court (2018) Yue Xing Zhong No. 159, filed a petition with this Court for retrial in the case concerning the formulation and approval of the overall land use planning by the respondents, Suixi County People's Government, Suixi County Housing and Urban-Rural Planning and Construction Bureau (hereinafter referred to as Suixi Housing and Construction Bureau), and the third party at first instance, Guangdong Beibu Gulf Agricultural Products Wholesale Center Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guangdong Beibu Gulf Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to examine this case. The examination is now concluded.

The court of first instance held that: Article 17, paragraph 1 of the Land Administration Law of the PRC provides: "People's governments at all levels shall organize the formulation of overall land use planning based on the requirements of national economic and social development plans, land consolidation, and resource and environmental protection, the land supply capacity, and the need for various constructions for land." Urban and rural overall planning refers to a comprehensive arrangement and specific plan within a certain period, formulated by the people's government based on the national economic and social development plan, as well as the local natural environment, resource conditions, historical circumstances, current characteristics, overall consideration, and comprehensive deployment, for the purpose of determining the scale and development direction of the city and countryside, realizing the economic and social development goals of the city and countryside, rationally utilizing urban and rural land, and coordinating the spatial layout of the city and countryside. It is a planned act directed at an unspecified majority and has universal applicability and binding force. According to Article 13, item (2) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the people's courts shall not accept administrative lawsuits filed by citizens, legal persons, or other organizations against administrative regulations, rules, or decisions and orders with universal binding force formulated and issued by administrative organs. Therefore, Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company's lawsuit requesting confirmation that the formulation of the "Overall Planning of Lingbei Town, Suixi County (2012-2030)" by Suixi Housing and Construction Bureau and Suixi County People's Government was illegal and requesting its revocation does not fall within the scope of administrative litigation accepted by the people's courts. Pursuant to Article 49, item (4) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 3, paragraph 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, citizens, legal persons, or other organizations initiating administrative litigation must have a case that falls within the scope of acceptance of the people's courts; if a case that has been filed does not meet the conditions for prosecution, the lawsuit shall be dismissed by ruling. Accordingly, the court of first instance, based on Articles 12, 13(2), and 49(4) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 3, paragraph 1 of the aforementioned interpretation, ruled to dismiss Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company's lawsuit.

The court of second instance held that: This case is a dispute over administrative planning. The contested "Overall Planning of Lingbei Town, Suixi County (2012-2030)" is a regional administrative planning formulated by the People's Government of Lingbei Town, Suixi County and submitted to Suixi County People's Government for approval and implementation, with the approval date being February 5, 2013. Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company's lawsuit challenging the approval act of Suixi County People's Government should have been filed within the six-month prosecution period stipulated in Article 46, paragraph 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC. However, Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company filed this lawsuit in March 2017, exceeding the statutory prosecution period. Accordingly, the ruling of the court of first instance dismissing Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company's lawsuit was correct in its result and is upheld. The reasons argued by Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company for setting aside the original ruling are not established and are not supported. The court of second instance, pursuant to Article 89, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, ruled to dismiss the appeal and uphold the original ruling.

Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company applied for retrial on the following grounds: (1) The land used by Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company complies with the planning, and all relevant certificates are complete, and it predates the land use permit, planning, and construction permit of Guangdong Beibu Gulf Company by many years. (2) The two respondents violated laws and regulations by granting land use planning and permits to Guangdong Beibu Gulf Company, creating serious safety hazards for production; in the event of an accident, the consequences would be unimaginable. In 2012, the respondents and Guangdong Beibu Gulf Company, without soliciting the opinion of the applicant, changed the planning for the surrounding land, including the factory area of Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company, and subsequently issued to Guangdong Beibu Gulf Company the Land Use Planning Permit No. 440823201400012 and the Construction Project Planning Permit. (3) The two respondents illegally changed the land use planning without any legal basis. After causing losses to Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company, they repeatedly made oral promises to provide resettlement and compensation but failed to properly resolve the conflict. (4) The courts of first and second instance failed to ascertain the facts in accordance with the law, the procedure was seriously illegal, and they did not effectively protect the lawful rights and interests of Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company. Article 50 of the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Urban and Rural Planning Law) provides: "After the issuance of the site selection opinion letter, the land use planning permit, the construction project planning permit, or the rural construction planning permit, if the lawful rights and interests of the permit holder are harmed due to the modification of urban and rural planning in accordance with the law, compensation shall be given in accordance with the law." The land use planning permit and construction project planning permit issued by the respondents to the third party have violated the above provisions, seriously harmed the lawful rights and interests of Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company, and created extremely serious safety hazards for production. The respondents have violated the relevant provisions of the Urban and Rural Planning Law. Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company's filing of this lawsuit did not exceed the statutory prosecution period.

Upon examination, this Court holds that the focus of this retrial examination is whether the act of the People's Government of Lingbei Town in formulating and the Suixi County People's Government in approving the "Overall Planning of Lingbei Town, Suixi County (2012-2030)" falls within the scope of acceptance of administrative litigation.

Articles 2 and 5 of the Urban and Rural Planning Law provide that urban planning and town planning are divided into overall planning and detailed planning. Detailed planning is divided into regulatory detailed planning and constructive detailed planning. Among them, the overall urban planning is a comprehensive deployment and spatial arrangement made on the basis of the social and economic development strategy of the city for a certain period regarding the nature, development scale, land use, spatial layout, and various urban infrastructure facilities of the city. It is the overall deployment and general outline for urban construction and development, possessing comprehensiveness, strategic nature, policy nature, long-term nature, and guidance. The formulation of the overall urban planning mainly considers local social and economic development conditions, natural conditions, resource conditions, historical background, and current characteristics, with overall consideration and comprehensive coordination. It falls within the category of public policy and norm formulation, with abstractness and uncertainty in implementation. Its legal significance lies in restricting the planning power at the lower level, rather than directly binding specific construction projects. The content of the overall planning needs to be implemented and concretized through regulatory detailed planning and constructive detailed planning, and further concretized through the issuance of administrative licensing decisions such as the "one document and two permits" (i.e., the site selection opinion letter for construction projects, the land use planning permit, and the construction project planning permit) for construction projects. Regulatory detailed planning is the interpretation and refinement of the overall urban planning in specific local areas, determining the land use nature, development intensity, and other control indicators for developable plots in specific local areas, as well as the spatial arrangement for road and municipal planning control requirements. It serves as the bridge between the overall urban planning and land development, and is the direct basis for administrative authority to manage construction projects. Constructive detailed planning is a specific and operational plan prepared based on the indicators determined by regulatory detailed planning for areas to be constructed, serving as the basis for the design and construction of various buildings and engineering facilities, and more importantly, as the basis for issuing the "one document and two permits" and planning management. Therefore, regarding the justiciability of the overall planning, the implementation of its content remains uncertain and requires detailed planning, especially constructive detailed planning, to be carried out, and further needs to be concretized through the "one document and two permits." A party who believes that the content of the overall planning infringes upon its lawful rights and interests shall seek relief through the objection procedures against the detailed planning that implements the overall planning, especially the constructive detailed planning, and through the judicial review procedure for the administrative act of issuing or not issuing the "one document and two permits." The supervision of overall planning may be conducted both through democratic deliberation procedures as provided in Article 16 of the Urban and Rural Planning Law, and through procedures such as professional judgment and public participation, but it is not appropriate to exercise supervision through judicial review procedures.

The formulation and modification of detailed planning may indeed affect the development and utilization of land by land right holders, or even diminish the land use rights and development rights lawfully acquired by the right holders. In particular, once regulatory detailed planning is approved, it becomes binding and is the most direct basis for planning management, serving as the statutory prerequisite for the transfer, development, and construction management of state-owned land use rights. The urban and rural planning department must strictly implement the planning in management, construction units must strictly construct according to the planning, and all relevant interest groups must comply with planning management. Therefore, there is also a need for judicial relief for the act of local governments in formulating and modifying detailed planning. However, unlike traditional administrative acts that only set the rights and obligations of specific administrative counterparties, detailed planning involves the overall spatial arrangement of large batches of developable plots in specific local area construction land and is highly policy-oriented and involves public participation. Judicial authorities should exercise caution in accepting and reviewing the legality of detailed planning acts. Generally, holders of specific land parcels should not be suitable to file lawsuits against the overall content of detailed planning. If a right holder files a lawsuit against content that has a direct stake in its land use rights, the people's court should still comprehensively determine the contested administrative act, the timing of the lawsuit, and the specific content and standards of review, taking into account the implementation of the detailed planning, the application for permits by the right holder or the opposing interest party, and whether the "one document and two permits" have been obtained based on the detailed planning. It is only appropriate to consider recognizing the justiciability of planning restrictions for specific land parcels in constructive detailed planning when the detailed planning has directly restricted the rights of the party and a clear conclusion of restriction can be reached without the need for the "one document and two permits" act; the counterparty must also specify clear litigation requests. The legality review of the content of detailed planning should respect the control of the overall planning and professional judgment, respect the policy adjustments of administrative organs, and consider the stability of detailed planning; the legality review is more reflected in procedural legality review. If the planning administrative department has already issued the "one document and two permits" based on the detailed planning, the party should directly apply for administrative reconsideration or file an administrative lawsuit against the act of issuing the "one document and two permits," or against the act of the planning administrative department failing to perform its statutory duty of issuing the "one document and two permits" administrative license, rather than applying for reconsideration or filing a lawsuit against the content of the detailed planning. If a party believes that the detailed planning infringes upon its land use rights, it may, pursuant to Article 7 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC and Article 53 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, request a concurrent review of the detailed planning in the reconsideration or lawsuit arising from the "one document and two permits" act to protect its lawful rights and interests. If the formulation or modification of detailed planning causes losses to the rights already acquired by the right holder, the right holder may also, in accordance with the spirit of Article 50 of the Urban and Rural Planning Law, directly sue the relevant entity for compensation in accordance with the law.

In summary, according to Article 13 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 2, paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the people's courts shall not accept lawsuits filed by citizens, legal persons, or other organizations against decisions and orders with universal binding force formulated and issued by administrative organs. The overall urban planning and overall town planning should not be included in the scope of acceptance of administrative litigation, to avoid conflicts regarding plaintiff qualification, prosecution period, legality review standards and intensity, and scope of res judicata under the current legal system framework. Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company's lawsuit against the act of the People's Government of Lingbei Town in formulating and the Suixi County People's Government in approving the "Overall Planning of Lingbei Town, Suixi County (2012-2030)" does not fall within the scope of acceptance of administrative litigation. The rulings of the courts of first and second instance dismissing its lawsuit and appeal respectively are in accordance with the law. If Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company believes that the planning administrative department's issuance of the Land Use Planning Permit No. 440823201400012 and the Construction Project Planning Permit to Guangdong Beibu Gulf Company infringes upon its lawful rights and interests, it may directly apply for administrative reconsideration or file an administrative lawsuit against the issuing authority, taking the relevant planning administrative permit as the subject of review.

In conclusion, Zhanjiang Xiqiang Company's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances provided in Article 91 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC. This Court, pursuant to Article 116, paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, rules as follows:

The application for retrial of Zhanjiang Xiqiang Industrial Gas Co., Ltd. is dismissed.
